intro: Healthcare social workers read people, coordinate care and solve complex problems. The closest of the 25 careers below are Occupational Therapists and advanced practice psychiatric nurses, both at an 84% match; occupational therapists earn a BLS May 2025 median of $100,330, or 48% more than the $67,880 healthcare social workers earn.
why_it_works: Helping patients and families through illness means assessing needs, arranging services and supporting people in hard moments. O*NET rates social perceptiveness at 4.25 out of 5 for this job, service orientation at 4.12 and coordination at 4. Therapy, nursing and counseling roles use the same skills. Every match needs no more education than you have, though many need their own license.
tips: Genetic Counselors earn $100,040, which is 47% more, and combine counseling with health science.
Teaching social work at a college pays $77,570, or 14% more, and suits experienced practitioners.
Check license requirements early; therapy careers need a specific degree and state license.

faq.q: What jobs can former healthcare social workers do?
faq.a: The closest matches are advanced practice psychiatric nurses (84%), Occupational Therapists (84%) and clinical nurse specialists (83%), based on O*NET 31.0. Recreational Therapists are 80% matched but earn $61,960, which is 9% less than the $67,880 healthcare social worker median.

faq.q: Which careers for healthcare social workers pay more?
faq.a: 16 of the 25 matches pay more. Physical Therapists earn $102,760 (51% more), Occupational Therapists $100,330 (48% more) and Genetic Counselors $100,040 (47% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. Each requires its own graduate program and license.

faq.q: Do healthcare social workers need another degree?
faq.a: Not more education in general: all 25 matches need no more than social workers already have. A master's degree is common, held by 87% of workers in the closest match, but therapy careers need a degree in that specific field.

faq.q: What skills should healthcare social workers build?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are instructing, troubleshooting, systems analysis and time management. Complex problem solving already rates 3.88 out of 5 for this job in O*NET, so teaching patients skills and analyzing systems are the main steps for most moves.
